---
title: "Kriging Interpolator"
date: 2026-09-17
categories: [tool, geostatistics]
description: "Upload sparse point samples (soil moisture, pH, pollution readings, anything measured at scattered locations) and predict a full continuous surface across the whole area — fitting a variogram model first, not just averaging nearby points. Runs entirely in your browser, powered by R."
page-layout: full
---

Upload a point file with a numeric column — soil moisture, pH,
pollutant concentration, anything measured at scattered sample
locations — pick that column, and this tool fits a variogram model to
how similar nearby points really are, then predicts a value everywhere
across the area, not just at the points you measured.

::: {.callout-tip}
**Private by design.** Your file is processed entirely in your browser
(R via WebAssembly) — it's never uploaded to any server, including
ours. Nothing to configure, nothing to trust: the code never gets the
chance to see your data.
:::

```{.webgeods-r #kriging-interpolator-example-r}
#| package: sf
library(sf)

# Deterministic synthetic soil-moisture survey: 45 sample points
# scattered across a roughly 800m x 600m field, with a real spatial
# trend (a band of higher moisture, as if following a shallow
# drainage line, plus a smaller ripple) and measurement noise on top
# -- gives the variogram real spatial structure to find, not just
# white noise a model could never fit meaningfully.
set.seed(42)
n <- 45

lon0 <- 12.4450
lat0 <- 41.8850
# Rough local meters-per-degree at this latitude -- only used to size
# the synthetic field in real-world terms, not a projection.
dlon <- 800 / (111320 * cos(lat0 * pi / 180))
dlat <- 600 / 110540

x <- runif(n, 0, dlon)
y <- runif(n, 0, dlat)

trend <- 22 + 10 * exp(-((x / dlon - y / dlat)^2) / 0.08) + 3 * sin(4 * pi * x / dlon)
moisture <- round(trend + rnorm(n, sd = 1.5), 1)

pts <- st_as_sf(
  data.frame(id = seq_len(n), soil_moisture_pct = moisture, lon = lon0 + x, lat = lat0 + y),
  coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326
)

st_write(pts, "/uploaded.geojson", driver = "GeoJSON", delete_dsn = TRUE)

"example soil moisture sample points written"
```

```{.webgeods-r #kriging-interpolator-inspect-r}
#| package: sf, geojsonsf, jsonlite
library(sf)
library(geojsonsf)

pts <- NULL
for (path in c("/uploaded.geojson", "/uploaded.shp", "/vsizip//uploaded.zip")) {
  pts <- tryCatch(st_read(path, quiet = TRUE), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(pts)) break
}

EMPTY_FC <- list(type = jsonlite::unbox("FeatureCollection"), features = list())

# A column counts as usable for kriging if it's already numeric, or if
# every non-missing value in it parses as a number (a common shape for
# a column read from a CSV-derived GeoJSON, where numbers can arrive as
# character strings) -- text/categorical columns are excluded rather
# than crashing later inside variogram() with an opaque type error.
looks_numeric <- function(v) {
  if (is.numeric(v)) return(TRUE)
  if (!is.character(v)) return(FALSE)
  non_na <- v[!is.na(v)]
  if (length(non_na) == 0) return(FALSE)
  suppressWarnings(!any(is.na(as.numeric(non_na))))
}

crs_warning <- NULL
summary_out <- NULL
features_out <- EMPTY_FC

if (!is.null(pts)) {
  original_crs <- st_crs(pts)
  if (is.na(original_crs)) {
    pts <- st_set_crs(pts, 4326)
    crs_warning <- "No CRS found in the uploaded file — assuming WGS84 (EPSG:4326)."
    original_crs_label <- "Unknown (assumed WGS84)"
  } else {
    original_crs_label <- if (!is.na(original_crs$epsg)) paste0("EPSG:", original_crs$epsg) else original_crs$input
    if (is.na(original_crs$epsg) || original_crs$epsg != 4326) {
      pts <- st_transform(pts, 4326)
    }
  }

  geom_col <- attr(pts, "sf_column")
  cols <- setdiff(names(pts), geom_col)
  numeric_cols <- cols[sapply(cols, function(c) looks_numeric(pts[[c]]))]

  # Preview coloring: pick a default numeric column the same way
  # Compute's own "Value column" input defaults (prefer
  # "soil_moisture_pct", else the first numeric column found), so the
  # map shows a meaningful preview immediately after Upload/Load
  # example -- before the user has touched that selector at all, same
  # as this tool's companion article, which has no column picker and
  # colors its points the moment its one compute cell runs.
  preview_col <- if ("soil_moisture_pct" %in% numeric_cols) {
    "soil_moisture_pct"
  } else if (length(numeric_cols) > 0) {
    numeric_cols[1]
  } else {
    NA
  }

  preview_min <- NA
  preview_max <- NA
  pts_out <- pts
  if (!is.na(preview_col)) {
    preview_values <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(sf::st_drop_geometry(pts)[[preview_col]])))
    finite_values <- preview_values[is.finite(preview_values)]
    if (length(finite_values) > 0) {
      preview_min <- min(finite_values)
      preview_max <- max(finite_values)
      pts_out$.previewValue <- preview_values
    }
  }

  summary_out <- list(
    count = jsonlite::unbox(nrow(pts)),
    crs = jsonlite::unbox(original_crs_label),
    columns = cols,
    numericColumns = numeric_cols,
    previewColumn = if (is.na(preview_col)) NULL else jsonlite::unbox(preview_col),
    previewMin = if (is.na(preview_min)) NULL else jsonlite::unbox(round(preview_min, 3)),
    previewMax = if (is.na(preview_max)) NULL else jsonlite::unbox(round(preview_max, 3))
  )
  if (!is.null(crs_warning)) {
    summary_out$crsWarning <- jsonlite::unbox(crs_warning)
  }

  features_out <- jsonlite::fromJSON(sf_geojson(pts_out), simplifyVector = FALSE)
}

list(features = features_out, summary = summary_out)
```

The code itself isn't shown here — it's a fixed, non-editable
computation using `gstat::variogram()`, `fit.variogram()` and
`krige()` underneath. Want to see the same pipeline built up one step
at a time, and why this tool runs on R, not Python? Read
[Interpolating Soil Moisture with Kriging](/posts/kriging-soil-sampling.html).

```{.webgeods-r #kriging-interpolator-compute-r}
#| inject: [valueColumn, variogramModel, gridResolution]
#| package: sf, gstat, geojsonsf, jsonlite
library(sf)
library(gstat)
library(geojsonsf)

pts <- NULL
for (path in c("/uploaded.geojson", "/uploaded.shp", "/vsizip//uploaded.zip")) {
  pts <- tryCatch(st_read(path, quiet = TRUE), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(pts)) break
}
if (is.na(st_crs(pts))) {
  pts <- st_set_crs(pts, 4326)
} else if (is.na(st_crs(pts)$epsg) || st_crs(pts)$epsg != 4326) {
  pts <- st_transform(pts, 4326)
}

value_col <- valueColumn
values_raw <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(sf::st_drop_geometry(pts)[[value_col]])))
value_mask <- !is.na(values_raw) & is.finite(values_raw)
pts <- pts[value_mask, ]
values_raw <- values_raw[value_mask]

if (nrow(pts) < 5) {
  stop(paste0(
    "Need at least 5 points with a valid numeric value in \"", value_col,
    "\" to fit a variogram — found ", nrow(pts), "."
  ))
}

# Working/calculation CRS: a variogram fit on raw degrees would treat 1
# degree of longitude and 1 degree of latitude as the same real
# distance everywhere on Earth, which they aren't -- same UTM auto-pick
# (bounding-box center) as this project's other vector tools.
bbox <- st_bbox(pts)
center_lon <- as.numeric((bbox["xmin"] + bbox["xmax"]) / 2)
center_lat <- as.numeric((bbox["ymin"] + bbox["ymax"]) / 2)
utm_zone <- floor((center_lon + 180) / 6) + 1
calc_epsg <- if (center_lat >= 0) 32600 + utm_zone else 32700 + utm_zone
calc_crs_label <- paste0("EPSG:", calc_epsg)

pts_calc <- st_transform(pts, calc_epsg)
pts_calc$.krige_value <- values_raw

v_emp <- variogram(.krige_value ~ 1, pts_calc)

init_range <- max(v_emp$dist) / 3
init_psill <- var(pts_calc$.krige_value)
v_model <- tryCatch(
  fit.variogram(
    v_emp,
    vgm(psill = init_psill, model = variogramModel, range = init_range, nugget = init_psill / 4)
  ),
  error = function(e) NULL
)

if (is.null(v_model) || isTRUE(attr(v_model, "singular")) || any(v_model$psill < 0)) {
  stop(paste0(
    "Could not fit a ", variogramModel, " variogram model to this data ",
    "(often too few points, or no real spatial structure to find). ",
    "Try a different model, or more sample points."
  ))
}

v_line <- variogramLine(v_model, maxdist = max(v_emp$dist), n = 100)

# Prediction grid over the sample points' own extent, padded 5% on
# each side so the surface doesn't stop exactly at the outermost
# points. gridResolution cells along the LONGER side, same "cap the
# cell count regardless of extent" formula as this project's other
# grid-building tools (Spatial Classifier, e.g.).
bbc <- st_bbox(pts_calc)
pad_x <- as.numeric(bbc["xmax"] - bbc["xmin"]) * 0.05
pad_y <- as.numeric(bbc["ymax"] - bbc["ymin"]) * 0.05
gxmin <- as.numeric(bbc["xmin"]) - pad_x
gxmax <- as.numeric(bbc["xmax"]) + pad_x
gymin <- as.numeric(bbc["ymin"]) - pad_y
gymax <- as.numeric(bbc["ymax"]) + pad_y

longer_side <- max(gxmax - gxmin, gymax - gymin, 1e-6)
cell_size <- longer_side / as.numeric(gridResolution)
nx <- max(2, ceiling((gxmax - gxmin) / cell_size))
ny <- max(2, ceiling((gymax - gymin) / cell_size))

xs <- seq(gxmin, gxmax, length.out = nx)
# Decreasing -- north (max) first: setRasterImage's own row-major
# convention puts row 0 at the TOP of the image, i.e. the northernmost
# row (see shared/map-raster.js), so the grid has to be built in that
# same order rather than relying on any later reordering.
ys <- seq(gymax, gymin, length.out = ny)
# expand.grid varies its FIRST argument fastest -- x cycles through a
# full row before y advances one step -- which is exactly row-major
# order with x as the column index and y (already north-to-south) as
# the row index. krige() below preserves this row order in its output.
grid_df <- expand.grid(x = xs, y = ys)
grid_sf <- st_as_sf(grid_df, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = calc_epsg)

k <- krige(.krige_value ~ 1, pts_calc, grid_sf, model = v_model, debug.level = 0)
pred <- as.numeric(k$var1.pred)
var_pred <- as.numeric(k$var1.var)

grid_bbox_calc <- st_sfc(
  st_polygon(list(matrix(
    c(gxmin, gymin, gxmax, gymin, gxmax, gymax, gxmin, gymax, gxmin, gymin),
    ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE
  ))),
  crs = calc_epsg
)
bb_wgs84 <- st_bbox(st_transform(grid_bbox_calc, 4326))

con <- rawConnection(raw(0), "wb")
writeBin(pred, con, size = 4, endian = "little")
raw_bytes <- rawConnectionValue(con)
close(con)
pred_b64 <- jsonlite::base64_enc(raw_bytes)

pts_wgs84 <- st_transform(pts_calc, 4326)
pts_wgs84$value <- pts_wgs84$.krige_value
pts_out <- pts_wgs84[, "value"]

result_out <- list(
  summary = list(
    count = jsonlite::unbox(nrow(pts_calc)),
    calculationCrs = jsonlite::unbox(calc_crs_label),
    valueColumn = jsonlite::unbox(value_col),
    variogramModel = jsonlite::unbox(variogramModel),
    nugget = jsonlite::unbox(round(v_model$psill[1], 4)),
    partialSill = jsonlite::unbox(round(v_model$psill[2], 4)),
    range = jsonlite::unbox(round(v_model$range[2], 1)),
    gridResolution = jsonlite::unbox(as.numeric(gridResolution)),
    gridCellCount = jsonlite::unbox(length(pred)),
    meanPrediction = jsonlite::unbox(round(mean(pred, na.rm = TRUE), 3)),
    meanVariance = jsonlite::unbox(round(mean(var_pred, na.rm = TRUE), 4))
  ),
  variogram = list(
    empirical = list(dist = round(v_emp$dist, 2), gamma = round(v_emp$gamma, 5), npairs = v_emp$np),
    fitted = list(dist = round(v_line$dist, 2), gamma = round(v_line$gamma, 5))
  ),
  raster = list(
    width = jsonlite::unbox(nx),
    height = jsonlite::unbox(ny),
    data = jsonlite::unbox(pred_b64),
    wgs84Bounds = round(c(bb_wgs84["xmin"], bb_wgs84["ymin"], bb_wgs84["xmax"], bb_wgs84["ymax"]), 6),
    min = jsonlite::unbox(round(min(pred, na.rm = TRUE), 3)),
    max = jsonlite::unbox(round(max(pred, na.rm = TRUE), 3))
  )
)

out <- jsonlite::fromJSON(jsonlite::toJSON(result_out, null = "null"), simplifyVector = FALSE)
# Attached AFTER the round-trip above, not inside it: sf_geojson()
# already returns finished JSON, and a second toJSON() pass would turn
# every scalar inside it back into a one-element array (same reasoning
# as spatial-classification.qmd's own compute cell).
out$samplePoints <- jsonlite::fromJSON(sf_geojson(pts_out), simplifyVector = FALSE)
out
```

```{.webgeods-r #kriging-interpolator-export-r}
#| inject: [valueColumn, variogramModel, gridResolution]
#| package: sf, gstat, terra, jsonlite
# Recomputes the same kriging pipeline (cheap relative to re-reading
# the source file) and writes it as an actual GeoTIFF via
# terra::writeRaster() -- in the CALCULATION crs (the projection the
# computation actually ran in), not the original file's CRS, since
# re-reprojecting the result back just for convenience would add a
# step with no real benefit -- the download button below labels this
# explicitly. Same reasoning and structure as
# viewshed-calculator.qmd's own export cell.
library(sf)
library(gstat)
library(terra)

pts <- NULL
for (path in c("/uploaded.geojson", "/uploaded.shp", "/vsizip//uploaded.zip")) {
  pts <- tryCatch(st_read(path, quiet = TRUE), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(pts)) break
}
if (is.na(st_crs(pts))) {
  pts <- st_set_crs(pts, 4326)
} else if (is.na(st_crs(pts)$epsg) || st_crs(pts)$epsg != 4326) {
  pts <- st_transform(pts, 4326)
}

value_col <- valueColumn
values_raw <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(sf::st_drop_geometry(pts)[[value_col]])))
value_mask <- !is.na(values_raw) & is.finite(values_raw)
pts <- pts[value_mask, ]
values_raw <- values_raw[value_mask]

bbox <- st_bbox(pts)
center_lon <- as.numeric((bbox["xmin"] + bbox["xmax"]) / 2)
center_lat <- as.numeric((bbox["ymin"] + bbox["ymax"]) / 2)
utm_zone <- floor((center_lon + 180) / 6) + 1
calc_epsg <- if (center_lat >= 0) 32600 + utm_zone else 32700 + utm_zone

pts_calc <- st_transform(pts, calc_epsg)
pts_calc$.krige_value <- values_raw

v_emp <- variogram(.krige_value ~ 1, pts_calc)
init_range <- max(v_emp$dist) / 3
init_psill <- var(pts_calc$.krige_value)
v_model <- fit.variogram(
  v_emp,
  vgm(psill = init_psill, model = variogramModel, range = init_range, nugget = init_psill / 4)
)

bbc <- st_bbox(pts_calc)
pad_x <- as.numeric(bbc["xmax"] - bbc["xmin"]) * 0.05
pad_y <- as.numeric(bbc["ymax"] - bbc["ymin"]) * 0.05
gxmin <- as.numeric(bbc["xmin"]) - pad_x
gxmax <- as.numeric(bbc["xmax"]) + pad_x
gymin <- as.numeric(bbc["ymin"]) - pad_y
gymax <- as.numeric(bbc["ymax"]) + pad_y

longer_side <- max(gxmax - gxmin, gymax - gymin, 1e-6)
cell_size <- longer_side / as.numeric(gridResolution)
nx <- max(2, ceiling((gxmax - gxmin) / cell_size))
ny <- max(2, ceiling((gymax - gymin) / cell_size))

xs <- seq(gxmin, gxmax, length.out = nx)
ys <- seq(gymax, gymin, length.out = ny)
grid_df <- expand.grid(x = xs, y = ys)
grid_sf <- st_as_sf(grid_df, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = calc_epsg)

k <- krige(.krige_value ~ 1, pts_calc, grid_sf, model = v_model, debug.level = 0)
pred <- as.numeric(k$var1.pred)

# expand.grid above cycles x fastest, y north-to-south -- exactly
# terra's own row-major convention for a matrix passed to rast()
# (row 1 = the top/north row), so no reordering is needed here beyond
# reshaping the flat vector.
pred_matrix <- matrix(pred, nrow = ny, ncol = nx, byrow = TRUE)
r <- rast(pred_matrix, extent = ext(gxmin, gxmax, gymin, gymax), crs = paste0("EPSG:", calc_epsg))
names(r) <- value_col

out_path <- "/tmp/kriging.tif"
writeRaster(r, out_path, overwrite = TRUE, filetype = "GTiff")
raw_bytes <- readBin(out_path, what = "raw", n = file.info(out_path)$size)
jsonlite::base64_enc(raw_bytes)
```

*First run loads the R engine — expect 1-3 minutes (R's WebAssembly
build is noticeably slower to start than this site's Python tools).
Instant after that, and again each time you come back to this page.*

<div id="ki-dashboard"></div>

<!-- Page-local, not site-wide -- same reasoning as spatial-classifier.qmd's
     own comment: only this one tool (so far) needs the ~828KB vega
     bundle. -->
<script src="/vega.min.js"></script>
<script src="/vega-lite.min.js"></script>
<script src="/vega-embed.min.js"></script>
<script src="/vega-chart.js"></script>

<script>
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {

  const KRIGE_RAMP = [
    [0.00, 166, 97, 26],
    [0.25, 223, 194, 125],
    [0.50, 245, 245, 245],
    [0.75, 128, 205, 193],
    [1.00, 1, 133, 113]
  ];

  // Same 5 colors as KRIGE_RAMP above, as literal MapLibre stops --
  // shared by the inspect-preview layer, the compute layer, and the
  // map legend below, so a point's fill is always the exact color the
  // surface would show at that spot, not a rough match. Bringing this
  // paint expression under a single function also fixed a different
  // problem: with a hand-duplicated 3-stop expression (the tool's
  // first version), most points -- anything near the middle of the
  // range -- rendered almost pure white, reading as "not colored at
  // all" against the light basemap. The heavier stroke keeps every
  // point visible as a distinct marker even at that near-white
  // midpoint, where the fill alone barely shows.
  const KRIGE_POINT_COLORS = [
    "rgb(166,97,26)", "rgb(223,194,125)", "rgb(245,245,245)", "rgb(128,205,193)", "rgb(1,133,113)"
  ];
  const krigeCirclePaint = (min, max, field) => {
    const step = (max - min) / 4;
    return {
      "circle-radius": 6,
      "circle-color": [
        "interpolate", ["linear"], ["get", field],
        min, KRIGE_POINT_COLORS[0],
        min + step, KRIGE_POINT_COLORS[1],
        min + step * 2, KRIGE_POINT_COLORS[2],
        min + step * 3, KRIGE_POINT_COLORS[3],
        max, KRIGE_POINT_COLORS[4]
      ],
      "circle-stroke-color": "#2a2117",
      "circle-stroke-width": 1.5
    };
  };

  const base64ToBytes = (base64Str) => {
    const binary = atob(base64Str);
    const bytes = new Uint8Array(binary.length);
    for (let i = 0; i < binary.length; i++) bytes[i] = binary.charCodeAt(i);
    return bytes;
  };

  window.kiChart = null;

  // Vega-Lite's text mark has no built-in background -- nugget/sill/
  // range sat as bare text directly on the chart's own gridlines.
  // Fixed the same way raster-gap-filler.qmd's own variogram panel
  // was: measure each label's real getBBox() after the chart renders
  // and insert a sized background rect behind it (same technique the
  // GeoStatistics articles' own hand-rolled d3 charts already use).
  // The one wrinkle found live building that fix: Vega-Lite's <text>
  // elements carry their OWN transform="translate(x,y)" attribute
  // (unlike d3's plain x/y-positioned text), and getBBox() returns
  // coordinates from BEFORE that transform applies -- a sibling rect
  // built from those raw numbers needs the identical transform copied
  // onto it too, or it renders offset by roughly the transform's own
  // translation instead of sitting behind the text.
  const pillifyReferenceLabels = (container) => {
    const svg = container.querySelector("svg");
    if (!svg) return;
    for (const t of svg.querySelectorAll("text")) {
      if (!/^(nugget|sill|range) /.test(t.textContent || "")) continue;
      const box = t.getBBox();
      const rect = document.createElementNS("http://www.w3.org/2000/svg", "rect");
      rect.setAttribute("x", box.x - 4);
      rect.setAttribute("y", box.y - 2);
      rect.setAttribute("width", box.width + 8);
      rect.setAttribute("height", box.height + 4);
      rect.setAttribute("rx", 3);
      rect.setAttribute("fill", "#fffdf8");
      rect.setAttribute("stroke", "#d8cdb8");
      rect.setAttribute("stroke-width", 1);
      const transform = t.getAttribute("transform");
      if (transform) rect.setAttribute("transform", transform);
      t.parentNode.insertBefore(rect, t);
    }
  };

  new WebGeoDS.Dashboard({
    tool: "kriging-interpolator",
    mount: "#ki-dashboard",
    layout: { sidePanel: { id: "ki-chart", flex: "1 1 280px", minWidth: "260px" } },
    upload: { languages: ["r"], kind: "vector", label: "📁 Upload" },
    example: {
      cellId: "kriging-interpolator-example-r",
      kind: "geojson",
      status: "✓ example soil-moisture samples loaded — pick the value column and Interpolate below."
    },
    emptyStats: [
      ["Points", "—"],
      ["—", "Upload a point GeoJSON/Shapefile or load the example above"]
    ],
    inspect: {
      cellId: "kriging-interpolator-inspect-r",
      layers: [
        // Colored the moment data loads (Upload/Load example), same
        // as this tool's companion article -- the inspect cell itself
        // already picked a best-guess default column (see its own
        // "preview coloring" comment) and returns its min/max under
        // v.summary, so this doesn't have to wait for the user to
        // touch the Value column selector or click Interpolate.
        { source: "kriging-interpolator-points-r", from: (v) => v.features, type: "circle", fit: true,
          paint: (v) => {
            const s = v.summary;
            if (!s || s.previewMin == null || s.previewMax == null) {
              return undefined;
            }
            return krigeCirclePaint(s.previewMin, s.previewMax, ".previewValue");
          } }
      ],
      stats: (v) => {
        const s = v.summary;
        if (!s) return [["Points", "—"], ["—", "Upload a point GeoJSON/Shapefile or load the example above"]];
        const rows = [
          ["Points", s.count.toLocaleString()],
          ["Original CRS", s.crs]
        ];
        if (s.crsWarning) rows.push(["CRS warning", s.crsWarning]);
        if (!s.numericColumns || s.numericColumns.length === 0) {
          rows.push(["⚠️", "No numeric column found to interpolate"]);
        }
        return rows;
      },
      // Shown from the moment data loads, using the SAME preview
      // min/max the layer above colors points with -- otherwise the
      // map would show colored points with no key explaining them
      // until Interpolate is clicked, even though the color scale is
      // already live. Replaced by compute.legend's own (slightly
      // different, post-kriging) min/max once Interpolate actually
      // runs -- see _renderLegend()'s own doc comment in dashboard.js
      // for why this field exists alongside compute.legend.
      legend: (v) => {
        const s = v.summary;
        if (!s || s.previewMin == null || s.previewMax == null) {
          return null;
        }
        return { gradient: KRIGE_RAMP, minLabel: `${s.previewMin}%`, maxLabel: `${s.previewMax}%` };
      }
    },
    compute: {
      cellId: "kriging-interpolator-compute-r",
      label: "▶ Interpolate",
      busyLabel: "⌛ Kriging...",
      inputs: [
        { kind: "select", name: "valueColumn", label: "Value column:",
          options: (v) => v.summary?.numericColumns ?? [],
          default: (v) => v.summary?.numericColumns?.includes("soil_moisture_pct")
            ? "soil_moisture_pct" : v.summary?.numericColumns?.[0] },
        { kind: "select", name: "variogramModel", label: "Model:",
          options: () => ["Sph", "Exp", "Gau"],
          default: () => "Sph" },
        { kind: "slider", name: "gridResolution", label: "Grid resolution", range: [10, 40], value: 25, step: 5 }
      ],
      layers: [
        { source: "kriging-interpolator-points-r", from: (v) => v.samplePoints, type: "circle",
          paint: (v) => krigeCirclePaint(v.raster.min, v.raster.max, "value") }
      ],
      stats: (v) => {
        const s = v.summary;
        return [
          ["Points used", s.count.toLocaleString()],
          ["Calculation CRS", s.calculationCrs],
          ["Value column", s.valueColumn],
          ["Variogram model", s.variogramModel],
          ["Nugget", s.nugget],
          ["Partial sill", s.partialSill],
          ["Range (m)", s.range],
          ["Grid cells", s.gridCellCount.toLocaleString()],
          ["Mean prediction", s.meanPrediction],
          ["Mean prediction variance", s.meanVariance]
        ];
      },
      // The map's own legend -- what the colors on both the surface
      // and the sample points actually mean, as a continuous gradient
      // bar (WebGeoDS.legend()'s own {gradient, minLabel, maxLabel}
      // shape, same convention raster-ndvi.qmd's article already
      // uses): both are colored by an interpolated ramp, not a fixed
      // set of categories, so a handful of discrete swatches would
      // misrepresent it. The chart alongside needs no legend of its
      // own: it's a plain distance-vs-semivariance plot with only
      // ever the same three series (points, fitted line, reference
      // lines), already named in its own title/axis labels.
      legend: (v) => ({ gradient: KRIGE_RAMP, minLabel: `${v.raster.min}%`, maxLabel: `${v.raster.max}%` }),
      // A GeoTIFF, not GeoJSON/JSON -- downloadButton()'s own
      // `getFeatures` shape doesn't fit, so this is the `raster`
      // variant instead (rasterDownloadButton()'s own shape, shared/
      // ui.js): the payload comes from running export-r (a hidden R
      // cell that re-krigs the surface with terra::rast()/
      // writeRaster()) and reading its result back, not from
      // serializing `value` directly. `prepare`'s own `inputs`
      // argument is `this.state.inputs` (shared/dashboard.js), which
      // only changes at the START of a runCompute() call -- always the
      // EXACT inputs the current result was computed with, never a
      // slider position nudged after Interpolate but before Download
      // that hasn't actually been re-interpolated yet.
      download: {
        raster: {
          label: "⬇ Download GeoTIFF",
          prepare: (value, inputs) => {
            if (!value) return false;
            window.valueColumn = inputs.valueColumn;
            window.variogramModel = inputs.variogramModel;
            window.gridResolution = inputs.gridResolution;
          },
          cellId: "kriging-interpolator-export-r",
          decode: base64ToBytes,
          getFilename: () => "kriged-surface.tif"
        }
      },
      onResult: async (v) => {

        const dashboard =
          WebGeoDS.Dashboard.find("kriging-interpolator");

        window.kiChart?.destroy();
        window.kiChart = null;

        if (!v) {
          await dashboard.map.removeRasterImage("kriging-interpolator-surface");
          return;
        }

        await dashboard.map.setRasterImage("kriging-interpolator-surface", {
          bounds: v.raster.wgs84Bounds,
          width: v.raster.width,
          height: v.raster.height,
          values: new Float32Array(base64ToBytes(v.raster.data).buffer),
          min: v.raster.min,
          max: v.raster.max,
          colorRamp: KRIGE_RAMP
        });

        // setRasterImage() always adds a brand-new layer ON TOP of
        // whatever already exists (shared/map-raster.js's own
        // addLayer() call takes no beforeId) -- moveLayer() with a
        // single id argument brings the sample points back above the
        // surface every run, so the actual measurements stay visible
        // rather than being hidden under the interpolated colors.
        const rawMap = dashboard.map?.map;
        if (rawMap && rawMap.getLayer("kriging-interpolator-points-r")) {
          rawMap.moveLayer("kriging-interpolator-points-r");
        }

        const empRows = v.variogram.empirical.dist.map((d, i) => ({
          dist: d, gamma: v.variogram.empirical.gamma[i], npairs: v.variogram.empirical.npairs[i], key: `emp-${i}`
        }));
        const fitRows = v.variogram.fitted.dist.map((d, i) => ({
          dist: d, gamma: v.variogram.fitted.gamma[i], key: `fit-${i}`
        }));

        const nugget = v.summary.nugget;
        const sill = v.summary.nugget + v.summary.partialSill;
        const range = v.summary.range;
        const maxDist = Math.max(range, ...empRows.map((d) => d.dist), ...fitRows.map((d) => d.dist));
        const maxGamma = Math.max(sill, ...empRows.map((d) => d.gamma), ...fitRows.map((d) => d.gamma));

        // range is very often the largest x value in the whole chart
        // (a sparse dataset's fitted range routinely exceeds its own
        // farthest observed distance) -- with a fixed "align: left"
        // label, that put "range ...m" starting AT the domain's right
        // edge and running off it, clipped by the side panel's own
        // width rather than visible. Anchored to whichever side keeps
        // it inside the plot, same logic the article's own d3 chart
        // already uses for this same label.
        const rangeNearRightEdge = range > maxDist * 0.75;
        const rangeAlign = rangeNearRightEdge ? "right" : "left";
        const rangeDx = rangeNearRightEdge ? -3 : 3;

        // A live-measured NUMBER, not "container" + "fit-x" autosize:
        // found live that Vega-Lite/vega-embed's own container
        // measurement is unreliable here specifically -- it reads 0
        // often enough to matter (an invisible, zero-width chart),
        // apparently racing against the map's own async resize
        // handling that runs right after setRasterImage() above
        // (shared/map.js's ResizeObserver reacting to the just-added
        // raster layer). A plain getBoundingClientRect() taken here,
        // synchronously, is not subject to that race.
        //
        // -50px: "autosize":"pad" below adds the y-axis's own label
        // gutter ON TOP of this number, not inside it -- passing the
        // panel's full width overflowed the panel by exactly that
        // gutter (~22px on a phone-width panel), found live auditing
        // this chart specifically after a live viewport resize/
        // rotation (Dashboard's own resize listener re-runs this exact
        // code at the new width -- see shared/dashboard.js's own
        // comment on it -- so this needed to hold at ANY panel width,
        // not just the one it happened to be authored against).
        const chartWidth = Math.max(200, (dashboard.sidePanelEl.getBoundingClientRect().width || 300) - 50);

        // No cross-linking need here (one map, one chart, nothing else
        // to select into) -- shared/vega-chart.js's renderVegaChart()
        // still requires a point-selection param and an externalParam
        // regardless (see its own doc comment), so this supplies the
        // minimum it asks for rather than a real interaction.
        window.kiChart = await WebGeoDS.renderVegaChart(dashboard.sidePanelEl, {
          "$schema": "https://vega.github.io/schema/vega-lite/v5.json",
          "title": "Empirical variogram and fitted model",
          "width": chartWidth,
          "height": 220,
          "autosize": { "type": "pad" },
          "params": [{ "name": "krigeExternal", "value": null }],
          "layer": [
            {
              "data": { "values": empRows },
              "params": [{ "name": "krigeSelect", "select": { "type": "point", "fields": ["key"] } }],
              "mark": { "type": "point", "filled": true, "size": 70, "color": "#42583c" },
              "encoding": {
                // Explicit domains, padded 5% past whichever is
                // larger -- the empirical/fitted rows, or nugget/sill/
                // range -- rather than Vega-Lite's own per-layer
                // domain inference: found live that a "datum" (not
                // "field") encoding on the reference-line layers below
                // does NOT reliably extend the shared scale the way a
                // field-sourced value does, so sill (typically the
                // largest y value of the three) could plot just above
                // the domain the point/line layers alone would imply,
                // clipped by the chart's own edge instead of visible.
                "x": { "field": "dist", "type": "quantitative", "title": "Distance (m)", "scale": { "domain": [0, maxDist * 1.05] } },
                "y": { "field": "gamma", "type": "quantitative", "title": "Semivariance", "scale": { "domain": [0, maxGamma * 1.05] } },
                "tooltip": [
                  { "field": "dist", "title": "Distance (m)" },
                  { "field": "gamma", "title": "Semivariance" },
                  { "field": "npairs", "title": "Point pairs" }
                ]
              }
            },
            {
              "data": { "values": fitRows },
              "mark": { "type": "line", "color": "#ab502b" },
              "encoding": {
                "x": { "field": "dist", "type": "quantitative" },
                "y": { "field": "gamma", "type": "quantitative" }
              }
            },
            // Reference lines for the same nugget/sill/range the stat
            // card already reports, in the same style as the article's
            // own hand-rolled d3 chart -- "datum" (a literal value),
            // not "field", since these three numbers come from
            // v.summary, not a per-row dataset column. Each rule gets
            // an EXPLICIT x/x2 (or y/y2) span rather than encoding only
            // y (or only x) for an implicit full-width/full-height
            // line: found live that Vega-Lite's "fit-x" + "width:
            // container" autosize resolves to width 0 for the whole
            // chart when any layer's rule has no x-domain-contributing
            // encoding at all to size against.
            {
              "data": { "values": [{}] },
              "mark": { "type": "rule", "strokeDash": [4, 3], "color": "#8a8378" },
              "encoding": {
                "x": { "datum": 0, "type": "quantitative" },
                "x2": { "datum": maxDist },
                "y": { "datum": nugget, "type": "quantitative" }
              }
            },
            {
              "data": { "values": [{}] },
              "mark": { "type": "text", "align": "left", "baseline": "bottom", "dx": 8, "dy": -4, "color": "#8a8378", "fontSize": 11, "fontWeight": 600 },
              "encoding": {
                "y": { "datum": nugget, "type": "quantitative" },
                "x": { "datum": 0, "type": "quantitative" },
                "text": { "value": `nugget ${nugget}` }
              }
            },
            {
              "data": { "values": [{}] },
              "mark": { "type": "rule", "strokeDash": [4, 3], "color": "#8a8378" },
              "encoding": {
                "x": { "datum": 0, "type": "quantitative" },
                "x2": { "datum": maxDist },
                "y": { "datum": sill, "type": "quantitative" }
              }
            },
            {
              "data": { "values": [{}] },
              "mark": { "type": "text", "align": "right", "baseline": "bottom", "dx": -2, "dy": -2, "color": "#8a8378", "fontSize": 11, "fontWeight": 600 },
              "encoding": {
                "y": { "datum": sill, "type": "quantitative" },
                "x": { "datum": maxDist, "type": "quantitative" },
                "text": { "value": `sill ${sill}` }
              }
            },
            {
              "data": { "values": [{}] },
              "mark": { "type": "rule", "strokeDash": [4, 3], "color": "#8a8378" },
              "encoding": {
                "x": { "datum": range, "type": "quantitative" },
                "y": { "datum": 0, "type": "quantitative" },
                "y2": { "datum": maxGamma }
              }
            },
            {
              // baseline "bottom" + a small NEGATIVE dy, not "top"/+3
              // -- found live (raster-gap-filler.qmd's own chart had
              // the identical bug) that placing this label just below
              // y=0 put it in the same band Vega-Lite draws its own
              // x-axis tick numbers in, overlapping them. Lifting it a
              // few px back inside the plot area clears them.
              "data": { "values": [{}] },
              "mark": { "type": "text", "align": rangeAlign, "baseline": "bottom", "dx": rangeDx, "dy": -3, "color": "#8a8378", "fontSize": 11, "fontWeight": 600 },
              "encoding": {
                "x": { "datum": range, "type": "quantitative" },
                "y": { "datum": 0, "type": "quantitative" },
                "text": { "value": `range ${range}m` }
              }
            }
          ]
        }, {
          selectParams: ["krigeSelect"],
          externalParam: "krigeExternal",
          keyField: "key",
          onSelect: () => {}
        });

        pillifyReferenceLabels(dashboard.sidePanelEl);

      }
    }
  });

});
</script>

<style>
#kriging-interpolator-example-r, #kriging-interpolator-inspect-r, #kriging-interpolator-compute-r, #kriging-interpolator-export-r {
  height: 0;
  overflow: hidden;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
  border: 0;
}
</style>

<div class="webgeods-closing-note">
First tool in the GeoStatistics family. The green dots are your own
sample points (brown = low, teal = high, on the same scale as the
surface underneath); the colored surface is the prediction everywhere
else. Want the code, or why this runs on R, not Python? Read the
<a href="/posts/kriging-soil-sampling.html">full article</a>. Got a
raster with gaps instead of scattered points — a cloud-covered
satellite band, say? The
<a href="/tools/raster-gap-filler.html">Raster Gap Filler</a> uses the
same variogram fitting, but fills an existing grid's own holes instead
of predicting one from scratch.
</div>

<script async data-uid="31051e3ca1" src="https://webgeods.kit.com/31051e3ca1/index.js"></script>
